newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 15.

text.p: Microsoft Corp plans to spend $400 million this year to develop content for its Internet services and nearly as much in each of the next few years, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
- Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co is interested in making a bid for DFS Group Ltd, a duty-free retailer.
- Life insurer PennCorp Financial Group Inc is expected to buy a smaller insurance company called Washington National Corp for $400 million or $29.50 a share.
- Great Universal Stores Plc agreed to buy Experian for $1.7 billion.
- Christopher Galvin will become Motorola Inc's chief executive office at the beginning of next year.
- U.S. consumer price index grew at a 0.3-percent rate in October.
- General Motors Corp will register a $170 million charge in the fourth quarter.
- DuPont Co will cut nearly 15 percent of the employees in its nylon business.
- Japan's Ajinomoto Co Inc pleaded guilty to conspiring with other firms to illegally fix the price of lysine.
- A weight-loss drug that works on mice might cause diabetes in humans.
- Some mutual-fund firms complain Dean Witter is not selling their funds as aggressively as it had promised.
- More companies are buying a once obscure form of insurance to help cover the cost of employee discrimination lawsuits.
- Copper traders acknowledge that the market's stability is exacerbated by problems in accounting for global copper output.
- A federal appeals court upheld for the second time a Baltimore ban on most cigarette billboard advertizing in areas frequented by children.
- Some insider trading cases might become more difficult for regulators to win.
- The FTC alleged that Automatic Data Processing Inc formed an information monopoly in the junkyard business.
- Canada and Chile have reached a free-trade agreement.
